Matching (3 stages, tried in priority order): (1) exact match against one of an item's declared `- test: <value>` lines, (2) a `::`-boundary suffix match against one (e.g. an item's `test: lock::lock_after_5` matches output test `tests::e2e::lock::lock_after_5`), (3) the stable_id->test-name-prefix convention (stable_id lowercased, runs of non-alphanumerics -> `_`, prefixed `test_`: REQ-001 -> `test_req_001`; compared against the last `::` segment of the test name, and the prefix must end at a word boundary — the name ends there or continues with a non-alphanumeric character — so REQ-1 matches `test_req_1` and `test_req_1_x` but not `test_req_10`). Stage 3 is used ONLY for an item with no declared `test` value (every layer-less item, and a layer item with no `test` attribute); an item with at least one declared `test` value is matched by stages 1-2 alone, never by the prefix convention. An item with at least one declared `test` value is only recorded when this ingestion's output covers *every* one of its declared values — a value with zero matches is reported in missing_refs instead, and that item is not recorded at all this call (a partial run must never look like a fuller not_run/pass/fail overwrite). Exactly one of output/output_file is required (output takes priority when both given). dry_run (default false) parses and matches without writing anything. commit defaults to `git rev-parse --short HEAD`; task_id is optional free-form linkage; executor_kind defaults to "ai". test_run_id (FR-304) optionally attributes this ingestion's run to a test run created via handoff_trace_test_run(action="create") — same additive runs/_latest.json by_test_run wiring handoff_trace_record's own test_run_id argument has. Returns a JSON string {run_id?,recorded,matched:[{item,result,tests:[string]}],missing_refs:[{item,test}],unmatched_tests_count,warnings,dry_run}.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

output.description: Raw test-run output (libtest JSON-per-line for cargo_json, JUnit XML for junit_xml). Takes priority over output_file when both are given.

output_file.description: Path to a file containing the test-run output. Ignored if output is given.

commit.description: Commit this run was executed against. Defaults to `git rev-parse --short HEAD` in project_dir (empty string if that fails).

task_id.description: Task this run is associated with, if any.

test_run_id.description: Attributes this ingestion's run to a test run created via handoff_trace_test_run(action="create"). No existence check against its definition file.

executor_id.description: Identifier of the executor (e.g. an agent id).

dry_run.description: Parse and match without writing any run file or test_refs update.

tools.name: handoff_trace_scaffold
tools.description: Generates one verification-layer item per acceptance-criteria bullet of a source (left-side) item (FR-305). Exactly one of items ([stable_id, ...]) or doc (a document slug/id — every item in it with an acceptance-criteria block) selects the source items; target_doc (required, a layer document's slug or id) is where generated items are appended. Each acceptance-criteria bullet becomes one new item: id = "<target layer's default id prefix>-<source id>-<AC number>" (e.g. "AT-REQ-003-1" from REQ-003's AC1, verifying an `acceptance` target_doc), body attrs `verifies: <source id>`, `from: <source id>#<AC label>`, `method: manual`. A `gwt`-kind AC (Given...When...Then) splits into a 手順 (steps, the Given/When clauses) and 期待結果 (expected result, the Then clause, also the heading title); an `ears`/`text`-kind AC has no distinguishable steps (手順: TBD, a fill-in placeholder), uses its full text as 期待結果, and its first 40 characters as the heading title. Idempotent: an AC that already has a scaffolded item anywhere in the project (a `from` value equal to `<source id>#<AC label>`) is skipped (reported in skipped, not regenerated) and does not count against limit. An id collision with any existing stable_id in the project is avoided by appending a single lowercase-letter suffix (`AT-REQ-003-1a`, `...1b`, ...; a warning is returned if all 26 are already taken). mode="preview" (default) computes generated/skipped without writing; mode="apply" appends the rendered Markdown to target_doc's body in one `doc_save(append_body=...)` call (which runs the real parser + layer sync), skipping the write entirely when there is nothing to generate. limit (default 20) caps how many new items are generated per call (skipped ACs don't count). If a source AC already has an implicit acceptance-verification item (a minimal-profile document's auto-materialized `<source id>#<AC label>` SubItem) with a recorded run, a warning notes that the run is not carried over to the newly scaffolded item. Returns a JSON string {target_doc,mode,applied,generated:[{id,from,title}],skipped:[{ac,existing}],warnings}. Requirement tree (SPEC-TREE-014): sources are leaves and composites/decisions with their own integrated acceptance criteria; a composite without any gets a warning pointing at its leaves.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

items.description: Source stable_ids to scaffold acceptance criteria from. Mutually exclusive with 'doc'.

doc.description: Source document (slug or id) — every item in it with an acceptance-criteria block is scaffolded. Mutually exclusive with 'items'.

target_doc.description: The verification-layer document (slug or id) generated items are appended to.

mode.description: 'preview' (default) computes without writing; 'apply' appends the generated items to target_doc's body.

limit.description: Maximum number of new items generated per call (skipped/idempotent ACs don't count).

tools.name: handoff_trace_suspect
tools.description: Derives and manages the 3 suspect kinds a V-model link/task/result can fall into when its upstream definition changed since it was baselined. action="list" (default, read-only): {suspects:[{kind:"link"|"task"|"result",item,upstream?,task?,link_type?,baseline_hash,current_hash}],counts:{link,task,result},unbaselined:{links,tasks},reverify:[stable_id,...],truncated}. `link` = a child's refines/verifies reference whose baseline no longer matches the upstream's current def_hash (or ac_hash for an `X#ACn` sub-reference); `task` = a task's requirement link whose baseline_hash no longer matches the linked item's current def_hash; `result` = a verification item's latest recorded pass whose recorded def_hash (or body_hash, for an older run) no longer matches. `unbaselined` counts references/links with no baseline yet (never suspects themselves — see action="baseline"). `reverify` lists Passing verification items whose own result is suspect or one of whose verifies links is suspect (does not change `state`). Filters: item, task_id, kinds (subset of link/task/result), layers, limit (default 50). action="clear": targets (required, array — each entry is one of {item,upstream} exact link, {item} all of that item's suspect links, {upstream} every link pointing at that upstream (bulk), {task_id,item?} task link(s), {layer} every suspect in that layer, {result:item} that item's result suspect), reason (required), evidence? ({run_id?,commit?,note?}), executor_kind (default "ai"), executor_id?. Moves each selected suspect's baseline to the current hash (a link's SubItem.link_baselines entry, a task's TaskLink.baseline_hash) — a result clear instead records one new carried-forward runs/<run_id>.json entry (reusing the last result verbatim against the item's current hashes; the authority for results stays runs-only). Writes one audit file per call to .handoff/trace/clears/<id>.json. Returns {cleared:{links,tasks,results},clear_id,baseline_suggestions,warnings} — baseline_suggestions is suggest-only (nothing is written): one entry per cleared task whose schedule has dates, {task_id,current_start,current_due,baseline_start?,baseline_due?,action:"set_recommended"(no baseline yet)|"update_recommended"(baseline differs from the schedule)|"manual_baseline_detected"(differing baseline on a pinned task, with a warning — not to be overwritten)}; apply one via handoff_update_task(schedule). action="baseline": migration helper for links/tasks that have no baseline at all — dry_run (default true) previews the count; scope? ({doc} or {layer}, omitted = whole project) restricts which unbaselined references are considered. Never touches an already-suspect link. Returns {baselined:{links,tasks,results:0},dry_run,warnings}.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

item.description: action=list: restrict to suspects about this stable_id.

task_id.description: action=list: restrict to suspects about this task.

kinds.description: action=list: restrict to these suspect kinds.

layers.description: action=list: restrict to suspects whose item is in one of these layers.

reason.description: action=clear (required): why this suspect is safe to clear, recorded in the audit file.

evidence.description: action=clear: optional {run_id?,commit?,note?} recorded in the audit file.

executor_id.description: Identifier of the executor (e.g. an agent id).

scope.description: action=baseline: restrict to {doc: "<slug or id>"} or {layer: "<id>"}. Omitted = whole project.

tools.name: handoff_trace_impact
tools.description: Read-only impact analysis for a proposed change (FR-404) — never writes anything, including _trace_report.json. Exactly one entry point is required: (1) item (+ optional proposed or proposed_file, a Markdown block that must contain that item's own heading line — a block without it is treated as "assume changed" with a warning) — parses the proposed text the same way a real layer sync would to get a hypothetical new def_hash/ac_hash; omitting both proposed and proposed_file means "assume changed" (a sentinel hash that reads as different from every real baseline, since no concrete new hash is known). (2) doc (+ required proposed_body or proposed_body_file, a full layer-document body) — every item common to both the proposed parse and the current corpus whose def_hash/ac_hash would change is treated the same way, for the whole document at once; any id the target document currently owns (including its materialized implicit-acceptance items) that the proposed body no longer defines at all is reported as a deletion instead (see `removed` below), for item mode scoped to just that one item and its own acceptance criteria. (3) file — the original req_impact entry point (shares its file-matching core with handoff_doc_req_impact): every requirement whose impl_refs/test_refs/scope_paths match this file is treated as "implementation changed" (no def_hash simulation, so would_suspect stays empty; only rerun_candidates is populated). (4) git_diff: true — same as file, but against every path `git diff HEAD --name-only` reports changed. Returns a JSON string {changed:[ids],removed:[{id,downstream_refs:[{child,type}],tasks:[ids]}],would_suspect:{links:[{child,upstream,type}],tasks:[{task,item}]},rerun_candidates:[ids],potential:[{id,depth}],truncated,warnings} — would_suspect only ever reports a downstream reference/task link that already has a recorded baseline (an unbaselined one is never guessed at); removed lists an id the proposal deletes outright, with its direct downstream references/task links (these would become dangling once the proposal lands, never suspect — there is no current hash left on the removed side to compare a baseline against; also echoed into warnings); rerun_candidates is every changed id's own verifying children (any verifies edge to it, regardless of baseline) plus a changed id that is itself a verification item; potential is a breadth-first walk over the same refines/verifies reverse-edge index starting from changed, reporting only depth >= 2 ("if the intermediate item also changed" ripple, informational only — suspects never actually propagate past one hop), capped by limit (default 50, truncated is true when more were reachable). Requirement tree (SPEC-TREE-013): tree_children_affected:[{parent, change:'changed'|'removed', children:[ids], would_orphan?:[ids]}] lists the same-layer decomposition children of every changed or removed item (a decomposition is not a hashed link, so children never become suspect — they are what to re-read); for a removed parent would_orphan is the subset left with no surviving parent (a DAG child with another remaining parent is not orphaned). Empty when no item has decomposition children.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

item.description: Entry point 1: a stable_id. Mutually exclusive with doc/file/git_diff.

proposed.description: item mode: a Markdown block that MUST start with item's own heading line (e.g. '### REQ-001 Title', then its attribute lines and body). The block is parsed like a layer document body, so without that heading the item is not found: the call then falls back to "assume changed" (sentinel hash) and adds a warning instead of computing a real hash. Takes priority over proposed_file when both are given. Omitting both means "assume changed".

proposed_file.description: item mode: path to a file containing the proposed Markdown block (same rule: it must contain the item's own heading line). Ignored if proposed is given.

doc.description: Entry point 2: a layer document slug or id (a non-layer document is rejected). Requires proposed_body or proposed_body_file. Mutually exclusive with item/file/git_diff.

proposed_body.description: doc mode (required unless proposed_body_file is given): the full proposed document body. Takes priority over proposed_body_file when both are given.

proposed_body_file.description: doc mode: path to a file containing the full proposed document body. Ignored if proposed_body is given.

file.description: Entry point 3: a file path. Mutually exclusive with item/doc/git_diff.

git_diff.description: Entry point 4: use every path `git diff HEAD --name-only` reports changed. Mutually exclusive with item/doc/file.

tools.name: handoff_trace_lint
tools.description: Read-only lint over the whole trace graph (FR-503/801; FR-504 added the quality rules and action="quality_prompt") — action="lint" and "quality_prompt" never write anything (the one write is action="nfr_check", below), E6 (in-memory-only resync of a directly-edited layer document, runs::load_latest_readonly, task_ids resolved from the task side without self-repair). action? ("lint" default | "quality_prompt" | "nfr_check"). action="nfr_check" (SPEC-RQ-001, ISO/IEC 25010 NFR checklist): classifies the selected requirements (items? = explicit stable_ids, default every requirement-layer item) into the 8 characteristics performance_efficiency / compatibility / usability / reliability / security / maintainability / portability / functional_suitability — an NFR-prefixed id is classified from its own segments (NFR-SECURITY-001, NFR-PERF-002) then from keywords in its text, any other item counts as functional_suitability, an NFR item that matches nothing is listed in unclassified. review? ({<category>: reviewed|applicable|not_applicable|not_reviewed}) records a judgement made from the prompt templates; recorded decisions persist across calls (not_reviewed clears one), otherwise status is derived: applicable when the category has items, else not_reviewed. Returns {categories:[{name,status,items:[stable_id],prompt_template (with a {text} placeholder),context}],unclassified,warnings} and — the only write this tool makes — merges {categories:[{name,status,items}],unclassified,scope,reviews} into .handoff/docs/_trace_report.json as `nfr_coverage` (the report is rebuilt first if absent; later `trace report` rebuilds carry nfr_coverage over). Unlike the other actions it takes the write lock for that merge. action="lint": Built-in rules (default severity in parens, overridable per id via config.toml's [trace.lint.rules] = "error"|"warning"|"info"|"off"): structural — unverified/unrefined/orphan/task_unlinked (warning), dangling/invalid_link/cycle/duplicate_id (error); change — suspect_link/suspect_task/stale_result (warning), unbaselined (info); tailoring — waiver_on_na/unlabeled_acceptance/invalid_waiver/unknown_acceptance_ref (warning), redundant_waiver/layer_outside_profile (info); drift (FR-801) — unsynced_body/task_link_dangling/attribute_after_body (warning), task_ids_drift/orphaned_legacy/orphan_run/id_like_heading (info); coverage gating (FR-202, info) — unwanted_coverage (a verifier whose layer is outside the item's effective needs — its own `- needs:` line or, when it has none, the project default profile's default_needs entry for its layer; the verifier is excluded from the item's coverage, so widen needs or move the verifier); quality (FR-504, info) — ambiguous_word (title matches a known vague term list, Japanese and English), missing_acceptance (a requirement-layer item with no acceptance-criteria block), passive_voice_hint (title matches a Japanese 「される」/「られる」 marker or an English "is/are/was/were + past participle" pattern); requirement tree (`parent` makes a same-layer decomposition DAG, so several parents are fine and there is no multiple_parent rule) — parent_cross_layer/parent_dangling/tree_cycle/self_parent (error), empty_group/kind_conflict/invalid_order/dotted_id/leaf_without_acceptance (warning), condition_missing (a decision/select child without a `condition` label)/condition_duplicate (two children of one branch parent share a label, trimmed and case-insensitive)/condition_on_non_branch (a label on a non-branch parent)/attr_unknown_parent (order@X or condition@X with X not in the declared parent list)/decision_arity (a decision with more than two children — use kind: select)/empty_branch (a decision/select with no children) (warning), shallow_leaf/id_parent_mismatch (info); format — frontmatter_invalid (error, unparseable _doc.*.md). Project-defined [[trace.lint.require]] policy rules (e.g. "approved P0/P1 requirements need a verifier": when={layer,priority,method,doc,approval}, need=verified_by|refined_by|implemented_by_task|passing|no_suspect|auto_test, severity default error) are evaluated alongside the built-ins, each producing its own rule id in findings. Input: rules? (restrict to these rule/require ids), fail_on? ("error" default | "warning" — which severity makes exit_code 1), format? ("json" default | "text", adds a rendered text field for CLI display), limit? (truncates findings, counts/exit_code still reflect every match). Output: {findings:[{rule,severity,item?,task?,doc?,message}],counts:{error,warning,info},exit_code,warnings,text?} sorted deterministically (severity descending, then rule id, then item's natural order). CLI `trace lint` exit codes: 0 = no finding at/above fail_on, 1 = at least one, 2 = usage/config error (unknown rule id, invalid fail_on, or any other handler error). action="quality_prompt" (E22: this server never calls an LLM itself — it only returns prompt templates for the caller, e.g. a session-loop AI agent, to fill and send to an LLM): items? ([stable_id, ...], present-but-empty is a usage error; omitted = every requirement-layer item), aspects? ([one of singular|verifiable|unambiguous|complete|feasible|traceable|necessary|implementation_free|consistent|completeness_set], ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148-aligned; an unrecognized name is rejected, not silently dropped; omitted = the nine per-item aspects, i.e. every one except completeness_set; completeness_set must be requested alone and returns ONE set-wide prompt {scope:"set",items_included,item_ids,text,aspects} that lists every selected item's title, statement and acceptance criteria, to judge what the requirement set as a whole is missing). Output: {prompts:[{item_id,title,statement,acceptance:[{label,text}],text,aspects:[{name,prompt_template,context}]}],warnings} — prompt_template contains a literal "{text}" placeholder the caller substitutes with the item's text before sending it to an LLM; text is the whole definition read from the document body as it is on disk: the title, then the statement (without its acceptance block), then "Acceptance criteria:" with one "- <label>: <text>" line per criterion (statement and acceptance are also returned separately; an item with no body of its own, such as a non-layer item or an implicit acceptance-verification item, gets its title only); context is a one-line explanation of what that 29148 characteristic means. The LLM's verdict is deliberately not recorded by any tool: it is advisory (it goes stale the moment the item changes and feeds no coverage, state or gate), so act on a fail by rewriting the item (handoff_trace_update upsert_item) and keep the reasoning in the conversation or a task note.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

action.description: 'lint' (default): evaluate built-in + [[trace.lint.require]] rules. 'quality_prompt': return LLM prompt templates for the 29148 quality aspects (FR-504). 'nfr_check': ISO/IEC 25010 NFR checklist (8 categories), persisted to _trace_report.json nfr_coverage (SPEC-RQ-001).

rules.description: action='lint' only. Restrict evaluation to these rule/require ids. Omitted = every rule.

fail_on.description: action='lint' only. Severity that makes exit_code 1 (CLI).

format.description: action='lint' only. 'json' (default) | 'text' (adds a rendered text field, for CLI display).

limit.description: action='lint' only. Maximum findings[] entries returned (counts/exit_code still reflect every match).

items.description: action='quality_prompt' or 'nfr_check'. Explicit stable_ids to generate prompts for. Omitted = every requirement-layer item.

review.description: action='nfr_check' only. Record review decisions per category, e.g. {"portability": "not_applicable"}. Persisted; not_reviewed clears a recorded decision.

aspects.description: action='quality_prompt' only. Restrict to these 29148 aspects. Omitted = the nine per-item aspects (every one except completeness_set). 'completeness_set' is set-level and exclusive: pass it alone to get one prompt covering all selected items (scope='set') instead of one prompt per item.

tools.name: handoff_trace_matrix
tools.description:
Read-only (E6, same fully-read-only load handoff_trace_lint/handoff_trace_impact use — in-memory-only layer-doc resync, runs::load_latest_readonly, task_ids resolved from the task side without self-repair) flat export of the whole trace graph as a CSV or Markdown table (FR-505) — handoff-vscode's matrix-export feature (t135) calls this instead of reimplementing CSV/Markdown generation itself (NFR-005). format (required): "markdown" | "csv". shape (default "tree"): "tree" is one row per top-level (root_layer) left-side item — INV-614's 'トレース表（行 = V字1本）' — with columns = every currently in-use layer (left side top to bottom, then right side top to bottom; a layer no item in the project uses gets no column) populated with that row's reachable descendants (refining children, and verifiers of anything in the row), plus a tasks column (every task with a requirement link to any id in the row, omit via include_tasks=false), then state (the root item's own aggregate TraceGraph state, already folding in every descendant) and suspect (the count of graph suspects whose relevant item is in the row). "edges" is one row per resolved refines/verifies link in the whole graph — {from,to,link_type,from_layer,to_layer,state (the from item's own state),suspect (true iff a link-kind suspect matches this exact {item: from, link_type, upstream->to})} — for import into an external tool; a dangling/invalid-level reference never appears here (handoff_trace_lint's dangling/invalid_link gaps cover those). root_layer (tree only, default: the shallowest-level left-side layer currently in use) must name a registered layer id; naming one no item in the project uses is not an error, it just yields zero rows. layers? restricts/reorders the column set to this list, intersected with (and reordered to match) the canonical in-use order — any entry that is unknown or not currently in use is dropped with a warning, never an error. A cell holding more than one id joins them with '; ' in CSV, '
' in Markdown (also how a literal embedded newline renders); CSV is RFC 4180 (every cell quoted, no BOM, LF line endings), Markdown escapes a literal '|'. output_file? is a path relative to the project directory (not .handoff/) to write the rendered content to instead of returning it inline — an absolute path or one that would escape the project directory (a '..' component) is rejected; this is the only write this otherwise fully read-only tool ever makes. Returns a JSON string {format,shape,root_layer? (tree only),columns,rows (row count),content? (omitted when output_file was given),output_file?,warnings}. Requirement tree (SPEC-TREE-014): shape=edges also lists the same-layer decomposition edges as rows with link_type 'parent' (child -> parent); when at least one parent row carries a branch label (the child's condition for a decision/select parent), a trailing 'condition' column is appended to every row (the label on labelled parent rows, empty elsewhere), otherwise the columns are unchanged. shape=tree, when the root layer has any parent edges, becomes a depth-first tree: a leading 'item' column holds the id indented two spaces per depth (Markdown output keeps the indent as  ), an id with several parents is starred ('REQ-A2*') and listed under each parent but expanded only once, and a 'parents' column lists each row's direct parents; a root layer without parent edges keeps the previous one-row-per-item shape and columns unchanged.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

shape.description: 'tree' (default): one row per root_layer item, columns = in-use layers + tasks + state + suspect. 'edges': one row per resolved refines/verifies link.

root_layer.description: shape='tree' only. A registered layer id to use as the row root. Default: the shallowest-level left-side layer currently in use.

layers.description: Restricts/reorders the column set to these layer ids (canonical order wins over the array's own order). Entries unknown or not currently in use are dropped with a warning.

output_file.description: Relative path (inside the project directory, not .handoff/) to write the rendered content to instead of returning it inline. An absolute path or one escaping the project directory is rejected.

tools.name: handoff_trace_next
tools.description: Read-only (E6, same fully-read-only load handoff_trace_lint/handoff_trace_matrix use — in-memory-only layer-doc resync, runs::load_latest_readonly, task_ids resolved from the task side without self-repair) ranking of "what to do next" across the whole trace graph into 10 kinds (FR-703; FR-307 added manual_pending; FR-204 added relink_candidate), each rank's detection rule and suggested follow-up call: 1 fix_failing (a verification item whose state is failing/blocked -> handoff_trace_slice then fix then handoff_trace_record), 2 review_suspect (an item with a suspect upstream link -> handoff_trace_impact then fix the body or handoff_trace_suspect clear), 3 rerun (a reverify or never-run verifier whose verified target is already implemented or beyond -> run the test then handoff_trace_ingest/handoff_trace_record) and manual_pending sharing the same rank 3 (an assignee-bearing item whose method is manual/visual/review and whose latest result is not_run -> handoff_trace_record), 4 write_verification (a left-side item WITH acceptance criteria whose horizontal coverage is uncovered or partial -> handoff_trace_scaffold into the pair layer's document, or handoff_doc_save creating that layer's first document when none exists; an item without acceptance criteria has nothing to scaffold and gets no candidate), 5 refine (a left-side item whose vertical coverage is uncovered or partial -> handoff_trace_update upsert_item dry_run adding a refining child in the next deeper layer's document, or handoff_doc_save creating that layer's first document; none for the deepest left layer), 6 create_task (a not_started left-side item with no implementing task yet whose vertical coverage is not already covered through its refining children -> handoff_trace_tasks), 7 fix_link (a dangling/invalid_link/cycle/duplicate_id/orphan structural gap -> fix the body), 8 baseline (an unbaselined refines/verifies reference -> handoff_trace_suspect baseline with dry_run=false, scoped to the item's document), 9 relink_candidate (a verifier or task still linked straight to an upper-layer item that a deeper-layer item now refines -> handoff_trace_update upsert_item dry_run rewriting verifies, or handoff_update_task rewriting requirement_ids; never proposes a link the verifier's level could not legally hold). Every suggest.arguments is valid against the named tool's input schema as returned (a record suggestion for a by-hand verification — manual_pending, or a rerun of an implicit/manual item — carries result not_run as a placeholder that MUST be replaced with the real outcome before calling: it is not a no-op, recorded as-is it writes a not_run run that supersedes a stale pass and clears its suspect). Within the same rank, ordering is deterministic: item priority (P0 before P1 before P2 before P3, unknown/missing last) -> the item's own layer level (shallower/upper first) -> stable_id natural order. task_id? narrows the candidate set to only that task's own requirement-linked items (same starting-set rule handoff_trace_slice's task_id branch uses). layers?[] restricts to items whose own effective layer is one of these, applied before ranking (never lets an out-of-scope item's candidate displace an in-scope one before limit truncation). assignee? restricts to items whose own SubItem.assignee matches exactly, applied the same way as layers?[]. kinds?[] restricts to these kind ids only (same 'present but empty is a usage error, unknown id is rejected rather than silently dropped' policy handoff_trace_lint's rules filter applies). limit? (default 10) truncates the final list; truncated reports whether more candidates existed. Returns a JSON string {actions:[{rank,kind,item?,task?,priority?,reason,suggest:{tool,arguments}}],truncated,warnings}. Requirement tree (SPEC-TREE-014): write_verification, refine and create_task candidates are only leaves and composites/decisions/selects that carry their own integrated acceptance criteria; a composite without them takes its coverage from its leaves, which carry the candidates.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

task_id.description: Restricts the candidate set to this task's own requirement-linked items only.

layers.description: Restricts the candidate set to items whose own effective layer is one of these ids.

assignee.description: Restricts the candidate set to items whose own SubItem.assignee matches exactly (FR-307).

kinds.description: Restrict to these next-action kinds only. Omit entirely to run every kind.

limit.description: Maximum actions[] entries returned (counts toward truncated, not a hard cap on candidates considered).

tools.name: handoff_trace_tree
tools.description: Read-only (E6, same fully-read-only load handoff_trace_lint/handoff_trace_next use) nested view of the requirement tree (decomposition DAG, SPEC-TREE-008). Built from the same tree index and sub-tree roll-up as handoff_trace_report(include_items) / _trace_report.json (schema v3), so the numbers always agree. root (an item id; an unknown id is an error) selects one node's tree; scope (an id prefix, e.g. "REQ-AUTH-") selects every item whose id starts with it, with the matching items that have no matching parent as roots; root and scope are mutually exclusive; with neither, the roots of every layer are returned (in-use layers first). layer limits the roots to one layer (an unknown layer is an error). depth (integer >= 0, default unlimited, 0 = roots only) bounds the expansion: a node below the limit keeps has_children=true with children=null. A node with several parents (DAG) is expanded at its first occurrence only; later occurrences have has_children=true and children=null (and are counted in totals.truncated_subtrees). filter keeps the matching nodes plus their ancestors (conditions are ANDed; each node's subtree roll-up is still the unfiltered value): state[] (passing|failing|blocked|not_run|uncovered, the node's own state), priority[] (P0..P3), suspect (true = only nodes with a suspect, false = only without), gaps_only (true = only nodes whose own state is uncovered or failing, that carry a suspect, or that have a tree-structure finding such as parent_dangling; not_run and blocked nodes are not gaps), kind[] (leaf|composite|decision|select). fields[] (own.<key> | subtree.<key>) trims each node's own / subtree objects to the listed keys; id, kind, parents, has_children, children and the branch labels condition/conditions are always returned, title/layer/doc/seq/order/priority are returned only when fields is omitted. Returns {roots:[{id,title,kind (leaf|composite|decision|select),layer,doc,seq,order,priority,condition? (the branch label of the edge from the parent this node is emitted under; omitted for roots and unlabelled edges),conditions? ({<parent_id>: label} for every labelled edge to a decision/select parent; omitted when empty),own:{state,dev_stage,approval,coverage:{horizontal,vertical},suspect (string[]: the distinct kinds link|task|result of the node's suspects, [] when none),tasks,acceptance_criteria (integer: the node's own acceptance-criteria count)},subtree:{depth,parents,children,leaves,state,dev_stage,approval,excluded,suspect,progress,tasks,all_tasks},parents,has_children,children:[...]|null}],totals:{nodes,leaves,composites,decisions,selects,max_depth,dag_shared,truncated_subtrees} (unique nodes shown),warnings}. An empty tree returns roots=[] with the DIAG-T001/T002/T003 diagnostics in warnings. Sibling order already reflects each parent's own order@ values — read children[] for order. CLI text output renders a node as `ID[*] [label] title (kind) ...`. CLI: handoff-mcp trace tree [--root ID | --scope PREFIX] [--depth N] [--layer L] [--filter-state S,..] [--filter-priority P,..] [--filter-suspect] [--gaps-only] [--filter-kind K,..] [--fields F,..] [--format json|text].

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

root.description: Item id to use as the single root. Unknown id is an error. Mutually exclusive with scope.

scope.description: Item id prefix; matching items without a matching parent become the roots. Mutually exclusive with root.

depth.description: Maximum expansion depth below each root (0 = roots only). Default: unlimited.

layer.description: Only roots of this layer. Unknown layer is an error.

filter.description: Keep nodes matching every given condition, plus their ancestors.

suspect.description: true = only nodes with a suspect; false = only nodes without.

gaps_only.description: Only nodes with a defect: own state uncovered or failing, a suspect, a tree-structure finding (e.g. parent_dangling, kind_conflict), or a wiring gap (orphan, dangling, invalid_link, cycle, duplicate_id). not_run and blocked nodes are work in progress, and unrefined / task_unlinked gaps are backlog, so they are not included (an unverified item already reads uncovered). handoff_trace_lint / handoff_trace_report list every gap kind.

fields.description: own.<key> / subtree.<key> entries to return. id/kind/parents/has_children/children are always returned.

tools.name: handoff_trace_test_run
tools.description: Test run definitions and dynamically-computed progress (FR-304). action="create" (default, write): scope ({layers?: [layer id, ...], kinds?: [one of fix_failing, review_suspect, rerun, manual_pending, write_verification, refine, create_task, fix_link, baseline, relink_candidate — same vocabulary as handoff_trace_next's own kinds filter], assignee?, items?: [stable_id, ...] — name the target items directly; combined with the other keys it narrows them, an id outside the matched set is skipped with a warning}), label?. Unknown scope keys and unknown top-level arguments are rejected. A scope that matches no items is refused (no empty campaign is created). Enumerates target_items the same way handoff_trace_next would for this scope: when scope.kinds is given, candidates are every item handoff_trace_next's derivation would surface for those kinds (needs the same full trace-graph build handoff_trace_next itself pays, PR-7 class); when scope.kinds is omitted, candidates are simply every layer item whose effective layer/assignee match scope.layers/scope.assignee (no graph build at all, PR-4 class); scope.items then keeps only the named ids. Persists the enumerated set, plus a generated test_run_id, to a new .handoff/trace/test_runs/<test_run_id>.json definition file (never overwritten, NFR-007). Returns a JSON string {test_run_id,target_items:[ids],total_target_count,warnings}. action="list" (read-only): limit? (default 20) — every test_runs/*.json definition, newest first. Returns a JSON string {test_runs:[{test_run_id,created_at,label,total_target_count}],truncated}. action="progress" (read-only): test_run_id (required) — filters runs/_latest.json's by_test_run[test_run_id] map (populated by handoff_trace_record/handoff_trace_ingest's own test_run_id argument) against the definition's own target_items and dynamically tallies progress; a target item with no recorded result against this test run counts as not_run (never cached, always recomputed from runs/*.json). An unknown test_run_id is an error. Returns a JSON string {test_run_id,total,executed,pass,fail,blocked,skipped,not_run,progress_pct,remaining:[ids],campaign_status,checklist_progress,warnings}. VERIFICATION CAMPAIGN (FR-512/SPEC-512): a test run is also a campaign with a checklist, campaign_status (draft -> in_progress -> completed -> approved) and progress {total,checked,pass,fail,blocked,waived,pending}. action="create" auto-generates one pending checklist row per target item ({item_id, acceptance_text (the item's description), result, evidence, note, verified_by, verified_at}) unless auto_checklist=false, in which case the checklist starts empty and a row is created the first time a target is checked (record_check/add_evidence), and complete requires every target to have been checked; its response also carries campaign_status and checklist_count, and list entries carry campaign_status and progress. action="get" (read-only): test_run_id — the full record incl. checklist. action="record_check" (write): test_run_id, item_id, result (pending|pass|fail|blocked|waived), note?, verified_by? (defaults to the calling agent), evidence? [{path,type,caption}] (appended; path must be non-empty and contain no '..'); the first non-pending check moves draft to in_progress. action="add_evidence" (write): test_run_id, item_id, evidence {path,type,caption} — appended without changing the verdict. action="set_status" (write): test_run_id, status — allowed transitions draft->in_progress, in_progress->completed (checklist must be non-empty with no pending item; fail/blocked rows are allowed — completed means every row was executed), completed->in_progress (reopen), completed->approved (approved_by required, and no fail/blocked row may remain: re-run it after reopening, mark it waived, or pass accept_failures=true to sign the failures off knowingly, e.g. for an inspection certificate that records a failed inspection); approved is terminal; draft is the initial state only and set_status=draft is always refused. action="delete" (write): test_run_id — removes the campaign definition (a mistaken or abandoned one); an approved campaign cannot be deleted. Runs already attributed to it stay. record_check/add_evidence are rejected on completed/approved campaigns. Campaign write actions return {test_run_id,campaign_status,progress,completed_at,approved_by,approved_at}.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

layers.description: Restrict to items whose own effective layer is one of these ids.

kinds.description: Restrict to items handoff_trace_next would surface for these kinds. Omitting this (or leaving it empty) uses the cheaper layers/assignee-only filter with no graph build.

assignee.description: Restrict to items whose own SubItem.assignee matches exactly.

items.description: Explicit stable_ids to put in the campaign. Intersected with the other scope keys; an id outside the matched set is skipped with a warning.

test_run_id.description: action=progress/get/record_check/add_evidence/set_status/delete (required): the test run / campaign to read or update.

auto_checklist.description: action=create: generate a pending checklist from the target items (default true).

note.description: action=record_check: free-form note replacing the item's note.

verified_by.description: action=record_check: who verified (defaults to the calling agent id).

evidence.description: action=record_check: array of evidence entries; action=add_evidence: a single entry. Each is {path, type, caption}.

accept_failures.description: action=set_status with status=approved: approve even though some checklist rows are fail/blocked (default false: such a campaign is refused). Use only when the failed result itself is what is being signed off.

limit.description: action=list: maximum test_runs[] entries returned, newest first.

tools.name: handoff_trace_propose
tools.description: Read-only suggestion of existing V-model items that may already cover a task, plus a ready-to-review Markdown template for a new one, sized to the project's applicable profile (FR-1004). Exactly one of task_id (loads that task's own title/notes/scope_paths) or title (+ optional notes, for a task that doesn't exist yet) is required. candidates: every persisted item's stable_id/title (SubItem.description)/layer, scored by a lexical+semantic blend (the same one handoff_memory_save's near-duplicate detection uses) between the query text (title, or title+notes) and each item's own title — no document body is read, sorted by score descending, capped at limit (default 5). proposal: the applicable layer set and implicit_acceptance is resolved [trace] layers (explicit config) > the project default [trace] profile > a 'standard'-shaped fallback when neither is configured (each fallback/assumption is reported in warnings, never silent) — the new item's layer is the deepest left-side (definition) layer in that set. When implicit_acceptance is true (a minimal-shaped profile), the template is one item at that layer with an inline "Acceptance criteria:" block (its own layer sync auto-materializes the verification item per criterion) — e.g. a minimal profile proposes one REQ- item. Otherwise the template is that item plus its paired verification-layer item (an explicit `- layer: <id>` override lets both live in the one proposed document even though its own default layer is the left one) — e.g. a standard profile proposes a SPEC- item paired with an ST- one. IDs are '<prefix>-<max existing number for that prefix project-wide, +1>', zero-padded to 3 digits; the prefix is the layer's default id prefix unless prefix is given (e.g. prefix: "CART" proposes the next free CART-nnn; it must be one of the target layer's registered prefixes — built-in defaults plus [trace.id_prefixes] — otherwise the call fails listing the allowed ones; ignored with a warning when parent is given). Every fill-in slot (statement, acceptance bullet, branch label) is the language-neutral marker TBD — replace it; the paired verification item is titled '<title> [<verification layer id>]'. doc is the layer document (matching the new item's target layer) whose scope_paths overlaps the task's own scope_paths (exact match or directory-prefix overlap, same classification handoff_claim_task's scope-conflict advisory uses); when none exists (including the title-only input, which has no task scope_paths to compare against), doc is instead a suggested (never created) new slug derived from the layer id and the query title, flagged in warnings. With parent (requirement tree, SPEC-TREE-011) the new item is instead a same-layer child of that item: id '<parent>-<next sibling number>', layer = the parent's layer, '- parent: <parent>' in the template; when the parent is a decision/select the template carries a '- condition: TBD' line (replace it with a label unique among the parent's children: yes/no for a decision, a case name or the reserved 'default' for a select) and a warning says so. Creation is out of scope for this tool — apply the proposed markdown yourself via handoff_doc_save/handoff_doc_update_section, or via handoff_trace_update's upsert_item op, only after the requester has reviewed it. Returns a JSON string {candidates:[{id,title,layer,score}],proposal:{profile,doc,markdown,next_ids}|null,warnings} — proposal is null when no left-side (definition) layer or reciprocal pair could be resolved for the applicable profile.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

task_id.description: Loads this task's own title/notes/scope_paths as the query and placement input. Mutually exclusive with 'title'.

title.description: Query title for a task that doesn't exist yet. Mutually exclusive with 'task_id'.

notes.description: Optional extra query text alongside 'title' (ignored when 'task_id' is given — the task's own notes are used instead).

prefix.description: Id prefix for the proposed item (e.g. 'CART'): the next free '<prefix>-nnn' is proposed. Must be a registered id prefix of the target layer (built-in defaults plus [trace.id_prefixes]); defaults to the layer's first prefix. Ignored with a warning when 'parent' is given.

parent.description: Requirement tree (SPEC-TREE-011): stable_id of an existing definition-layer item to decompose. The proposed item is a same-layer child of it: its layer is the parent's effective layer, its id is '<parent>-<n>' (n = highest existing '<parent>-<digits>' + 1, zero-padded to 3 digits), the template carries '- parent: <parent>', and the parent's own document is preferred as the placement. Fails when the parent does not exist or is not on a definition (left-side) layer.

tools.name: handoff_trace_tasks
tools.description: Generates one task per V-model item still missing the task role it needs (FR-605). Target selection: a left-side (definition) item with no task yet holding an `implements` link to it, or a right-side (verification) item with no task yet holding an `executes` link to it AND whose latest recorded result (runs/_latest.json) is not `"pass"` (an already-passing verifier needs no task). An item that already has a task holding the role this call would otherwise generate is idempotent — reported in `skipped`, never regenerated. Exactly one of items ([stable_id, ...], explicit targets — any id not found in the project is reported in warnings) or select ({layers?: [layer id, ...], gap_kinds?: [one of unverified/unrefined/orphan/dangling/invalid_link/cycle/duplicate_id/task_unlinked], dev_stage?: "not_started"|"in_progress"|"implemented"|"tested"|"verified"}) restricts the scan; omitting both scans every item in the project. Each generated task: title `"<stable_id> <item title>"` (SubItem.description), a `requirement_ids`/`requirement_roles` reverse link to the source item (role implements/executes, same inference `handoff_update_task`'s own create path uses when no explicit role is given), `labels: ["layer:<effective layer id>"]`, `scope_paths` copied from the item's owning document (not the item itself) — done_criteria are deliberately never copied (FR-603). parent_id (optional) makes every generated task a child of that task. estimate_hours is required when mode="apply" and [settings] require_estimate_hours is enabled project-wide (every generated task starts in status "todo", which handoff_update_task's own per-task estimate rule exempts, so this tool enforces its own upfront whole-batch requirement instead of silently creating unestimated tasks); when given, it is applied to every task this call creates. mode="preview" (default) computes without writing; mode="apply" creates the tasks via handoff_update_task's own shared create path (same validation: status/priority, done-guard pre-check, dependency validation, require_estimate_hours). limit (default 20) caps the number of generated/planned entries (skipped items don't count) — scanning is read-only (E6: in-memory-only layer-doc resync, runs::load_latest_readonly, task_ids resolved from the task side without self-repair), the only write path is the task creation itself. Returns a JSON string {mode,created|planned:[{task_id? (apply only),item,role,title}],skipped:[{item,role,existing}],warnings}. Requirement tree (SPEC-TREE-014): an implements task is only generated for a leaf or for a composite/decision with its own integrated acceptance criteria; a composite without them is left out (reported in warnings — create the tasks on its leaves instead), also when named in items.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

items.description: Explicit stable_ids to consider. Mutually exclusive with 'select'. Omitting both scans every item in the project.

select.description: Restricts the scan. Mutually exclusive with 'items'.

layers.description: Restrict to items whose effective layer is one of these ids.

gap_kinds.description: Restrict to items that have at least one of these handoff_trace_lint gap kinds.

dev_stage.description: Restrict to items whose own dev_stage equals this value.

parent_id.description: Every generated task becomes a child of this task, if given.

estimate_hours.description: Applied to every task this call creates (schedule.estimate_hours). Required for mode="apply" when [settings] require_estimate_hours is enabled.

mode.description: 'preview' (default) computes without writing; 'apply' creates the tasks.

limit.description: Maximum generated/planned entries (skipped items don't count against it).

tools.name: handoff_trace_update
tools.description: Bulk-mutation entry point over 7 op kinds in one call (FR-702/FR-601's remainder). Input: ops (required, non-empty array — each entry has an 'op' field naming one of upsert_item/link/unlink/set/record/clear_suspect/set_layer_status, see below), task_id? (default task: a link/unlink op that omits its own 'task' uses it; it is also the task the merged record run is linked to — record ops have no task of their own; upsert_item/set/set_layer_status ignore it, and clear_suspect never uses it as a default — that op's own task_id is a clear-target selector; with propose=true it is expanded into the delta's link/unlink ops), dry_run? (default false), executor_kind? ('ai' default | 'human'), executor_id?, commit? (used by record ops). E15 atomicity: every op — input shape, enum values (role: implements/executes, priority: P0-P3, result, dev_stage, approval), and every referential lookup this op kind commits to (document existence, upsert_item's after target and its own id resolving to a real item once rendered, link/unlink's item and task, set's item) — is validated, in ops' input order, before anything is written; an item lookup is checked against the union of the pre-call corpus and every id an earlier upsert_item op in the same call already planned, so a link/set op can legally target an item an earlier op in the same call creates. record's item is deliberately not existence-checked (it is forwarded to handoff_trace_record, which already records an unresolvable item with a warning rather than rejecting it — trace_update does not impose a stricter policy than the single-op tool). If any op fails validation, nothing is written and the response's failed names that op (by its 0-based position in the input ops array, not execution order). Writes then run in the fixed category order §4.8/E15 specify regardless of input order — 本文 (upsert_item) -> リンク (link/unlink) -> 実行時データ (set) -> 記録 (record) -> 解除 (clear_suspect) — and a write-time failure (rare: an IO/optimistic-lock error) stops before the next category, returning applied for whatever already landed on disk (this tool never attempts a cross-file rollback, E15: 'ファイルをまたぐトランザクションにはしない'). upsert_item {doc, id, title?, statement?, acceptance?: [{label,text}], attrs?: {layer,refines,verifies,parent,order,"order@<parent_id>",kind,condition,"condition@<parent_id>",priority,method,test,rationale,derived,"waive-verify","waive-refine",needs,assignee}, after?}: rewrites one item in a layer document's body (§2.2 notation, rendered via the same src/storage/docs/layer_render.rs trace_scaffold uses). An existing item (matched by id in doc's current body) has only the parts actually given replaced — omitted title/statement/acceptance/attrs sub-keys keep the item's current value (attrs is merged key-by-key, not replaced as a whole block, so an existing rationale/derived/waiver/assignee/needs attribute the op doesn't mention survives untouched; attrs.assignee = single-line roster key and attrs.needs = comma-separated layer ids or an array (an empty array = explicit 'no coverage needed'), both cleared by "" or null; an attrs key outside the list above is ignored with an 'unknown attrs key' warning). An op-level key the op kind does not read is likewise ignored with an 'unknown key' warning (ops[i]: unknown key '...' on a <op> op was ignored). acceptance, when given, REPLACES the item's whole criteria list (not a label-wise merge): every existing criterion missing from it is deleted, and an 'acceptance_dropped: ...' warning names each dropped label plus any verifier of <id>#<label> (with its latest recorded result) that is left dangling — re-send every criterion to keep; a malformed acceptance entry (not {label,text} strings) fails validation; requirement-tree attrs: parent = same-layer parent id(s), comma-separated string or array (several parents make a DAG; "" clears), order = non-negative integer sibling order, order@<parent_id> = per-parent order, kind = leaf|group|decision|select ("" clears; select = N-way branch), condition = single-line branch label shown on the edge from a decision/select parent (default for every parent, trimmed; "" clears), condition@<parent_id> = per-parent label overriding condition (the label is part of the item's definition hash); the <parent_id> of order@/condition@ must be in the item's declared parent list after the op is merged (a not-yet-existing parent is fine) — a violating op is rejected with an error telling you to add the target to attrs.parent or clear the key — validated before anything is written, an op that names a nonexistent / other-layer / self parent, closes a parent cycle (also through earlier ops of the same call), uses a dotted id (DSP-1.2.3), or creates an id another document already owns fails with failed.errors:[{code: dotted_id|duplicate_id|self_parent|parent_dangling|parent_cross_layer|tree_cycle, item, message, path? (tree_cycle: the closed path)}]; a non-existent id creates a new item after the 'after' id (or at the document's end when 'after' is omitted — an 'after' id that does not resolve to an item in the document's current body fails validation). Writing a new/changed derived or waive-verify/waive-refine value (including a brand-new item created with one already set, and including changing an existing reason) always adds a 'waiver_added: <id> <axis> <reason>' line to warnings (E4 — never a silent AI-side waiver, not even via creation). A non-existent id's prefix must still match this document's layer configuration (§2.2's grammar) — an id that cannot form a recognized item heading fails validation instead of silently writing a heading no reader will ever recognize as an item. Multiple upsert_item ops targeting different documents in the same call are batch-synced together (local sync in memory for every touched document, then cross-document link_baselines resolved against that same in-memory state — never a stale on-disk read) so a same-call upstream item's brand-new hash — not a stale on-disk one — becomes a same-call downstream item's new refines/verifies link_baselines entry (§2.5 step 4); each touched document is still written to disk exactly once, under its own optimistic-lock check. link/unlink {item, task?, role?}: adds/removes a requirement-type task_links entry via the same task-side-primary path handoff_update_task(requirement_ids=...) uses (docs::apply_requirement_diff_and_propagate — role, when given, must be 'implements' or 'executes'; omitted is inferred from the item's category, same as that path); item must resolve (pre-call corpus or an id upserted earlier in the same call) or the op fails validation. multiple ops for the same task are merged into one task-file read-modify-write. set {item, dev_stage?, approval?, impl_refs?, priority?, test_refs?}: (impl_refs/test_refs = non-empty array of {path, lines?, label?} objects replacing the stored list; a malformed entry fails validation and changes nothing; an empty array is a no-op with a warning; null clears) writes an item's runtime fields directly — dev_stage/approval/impl_refs work on any item; priority (P0-P3 only) /test_refs only on a non-layer item (a layer item's priority/test_refs are body-owned, §2.3 — rejected with an error naming the guard). approval is one of draft/review/approved (any transition is accepted; the current value is not checked) and writes SubItem.approval only — status/verified_at are never touched. approval="approved" additionally stamps approved_hash (the item's current def_hash — direct-edited layer documents are re-synced first so it is the fresh one), approved_by (executor_id, absent when not given) and approved_at, and writes one audit record under .handoff/trace/approvals/<id>.json per call; a later definition change rolls the approval back automatically. draft and review write just the approval value (no hash/by/at, no audit file). FR-522 waiver record: waive_reason + waive_approved_by (both non-empty strings given together, or both null to clear) store a structured waiver on the item (SubItem.waive_reason/waive_approved_by — a runtime record that survives layer re-sync, surfaced as items[].waive:{reason,approved_by} in handoff_trace_report; it does not itself change coverage, which stays driven by the body's waive-verify/waive-refine); recording one always adds a 'waiver_added: <id> waive <reason>' line to warnings. At least one of dev_stage/approval/impl_refs/priority/test_refs/waive_reason+waive_approved_by must be given. BUG FLOW (FR-522): record fail -> the layer demotes automatically (FR-510); open a bug via handoff_update_task(labels=["bug", "bug:<fix|defer|waive|not_a_bug>"], requirement_ids=[...]); fix, then edit/re-verify (suspect/reverify) and record pass; for a waive disposition, record the waiver with this set op. record {item, result, note?, evidence?}: every record op across the whole call is merged into exactly one runs/<id>.json file via handoff_trace_record (result must be one of pass/fail/blocked/not_run/skipped). clear_suspect {item?, upstream?, task_id?, layer?, result?, reason}: one of the clear-target shapes ({item,upstream} one link, {item} all of that item's suspect links, {upstream} every link pointing at it, {task_id, item?} task link(s), {layer} every suspect in that layer, {result} that item's result suspect) plus reason (required) — delegates to handoff_trace_suspect(action="clear") exactly once per clear_suspect op (one audit file per op, same .handoff/trace/clears/<id>.json convention). set_layer_status {layer, status} (FR-510, SPEC-510): explicit layer review operation — status is one of under_review/approved/reset; under_review and approved require the layer's derived status to be verified (all items passing, no gap attributed to the layer), checked after every other op of the call has been applied, and reset drops the explicit record (the layer reverts to its derived status). Applied last, persisted in .handoff/trace/layer_status.json, and followed by a refresh of _trace_report.json (layer_statuses/project_status); an approved/under_review layer that stops being verified is demoted automatically by the next handoff_trace_report. Not allowed in propose=true. dry_run=true skips every write and returns the same applied shape as a preview: for upsert_item, result.diff is a unified-diff hunk (@@ -start,oldlen +start,newlen @@) scoped to exactly the lines that op would change (not a whole-document diff) — every other op kind's result previews its resolved arguments. Returns a JSON string {applied:[{op_index,op,result}],failed?:{op_index,error},warnings,suspect_introduced?} (dry_run response additionally sets dry_run:true) — suspect_introduced (upsert_item only, same shape doc_save's own field uses) is present whenever at least one upsert_item changed an item's def_hash. propose=true (FR-407; mutually exclusive with dry_run) runs this same phase-1 validation and preview generation but, instead of discarding it (dry_run) or writing it to the document, persists it as a new pending handoff_trace_delta — only upsert_item/link/unlink/set ops are allowed in a propose call (record/clear_suspect are rejected before validation even starts, same restriction handoff_trace_delta(action="create") enforces); description? is forwarded to the created delta. Returns {delta_id,ops_count,previews:[{op_index,diff}],warnings,propose:true} — use handoff_trace_delta(action="apply"|"reject") to resolve it later. SPEC-TREE-012/013: when a touched document changed on disk between validation and the write (optimistic-lock conflict), every op is re-validated and re-applied against the latest state, up to 3 retries with 10/20/40 ms backoff (before anything was written, so audit files for record/clear_suspect are never duplicated); a conflict that persists fails with the usual 'changed on disk' error. The response also carries orphaned_children:[stable_id] — decomposition children left with no surviving parent because an item disappeared from a touched document (a DAG child with another remaining parent is not orphaned; normally empty, since upsert_item never removes an item).

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

ops.description: Non-empty array of ops, each with an 'op' field naming one of upsert_item/link/unlink/set/record/clear_suspect/set_layer_status, plus that op's own arguments (see this tool's description).

task_id.description: Default task: used by a link/unlink op that omits its own 'task', and the task the merged record run is linked to. Not applied to upsert_item/set/set_layer_status; clear_suspect's own task_id is a clear-target selector, not a default. With propose=true it is expanded into the delta's link/unlink ops.

dry_run.description: Validate and preview every op (including a unified-diff hunk per upsert_item) without writing anything. Mutually exclusive with 'propose'.

propose.description: Run the same phase-1 validation and preview as dry_run, but persist the result as a new pending handoff_trace_delta (FR-407) instead of discarding it or writing it to the document. Only upsert_item/link/unlink/set ops are allowed (record/clear_suspect are rejected up front). Mutually exclusive with 'dry_run'.

description.description: propose=true: free-form description of what this delta proposes (forwarded to the created delta).

executor_id.description: Identifier of the executor (e.g. an agent id).

commit.description: Commit used by record ops (passed through to handoff_trace_record).

tools.name: handoff_task_checklist
tools.description: action="view" (default, and only supported action — action="generate" was removed; use handoff_trace_scaffold instead): pure-view aggregation of a task's done_criteria and its linked documents' verification matrices. No new data is written — reads task_links (link_type="doc") and each linked document's verification matrix, computed fresh on every call. Returns {task_id,title,no_linked_docs:true,trace} as a fast-path response when the task has no linked documents. Otherwise returns {task_id,title,no_linked_docs:false,done_criteria:{items:[…],progress:{…}},verification_coverage:{documents:[{doc_id,slug,title,doc_type,items:[{fragment_seq,heading,status,stale,visual_state,impl_refs,test_refs}],progress:{…}}],overall:{…}},combined_readiness:{done_criteria_met,verification_complete,ready,blockers:[{type:"criteria"|"verification",…}]},suggested_actions:[…],trace}. trace is {layers,blockers} from this task's requirement-type task_links (independent of the doc-type links above), or null when it has none — same shape and read-only (E6) contract as handoff_get_task's trace field. Each item's visual_state is computed in priority order stale > skipped > verified > implemented (pending+impl_refs+test_refs) > in_progress (pending+impl_refs only) > untouched.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

task_id.description: Task ID to build the checklist for (e.g. 't1', 't1.2').

tools.name: handoff_claim_task
tools.description: Claim a task for exclusive work, guarded by a cross-process file lock (flock). Fails if the task is already claimed by another agent with a non-expired lease; an expired lease is silently taken over. A todo/blocked task moves to in_progress. Returns the updated task JSON, including the new lock. If the claimed task's scope_paths overlap another active (in_progress, locked) task's scope_paths, an advisory 'warnings' array is included ({level:"info"|"warn", message}) — same-directory overlap is 'info', same-file overlap is 'warn'. Warnings never block the claim.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

task_id.description: Task ID to claim (e.g. 't1', 't1.2').

session_id.description: Session ID claiming the task, recorded on the lock for diagnostics.

lease_ttl.description: Lease duration in seconds before the claim expires and can be taken over. Defaults to 1800 (30 minutes).

tools.name: handoff_release_task
tools.description: Release a task previously claimed by this agent, clearing its lock and reverting its status. Fails if the task's lock is held by a different agent.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

task_id.description: Task ID to release.

reason.description: Optional free-text reason for releasing, echoed back in the response.

revert_status.description: Status to revert the task to after releasing.

tools.name: handoff_list_agents
tools.description: List registered agents across worktrees (`.handoff/agents/`), with freshly-computed active/stale/disconnected status based on heartbeat age.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

status.description: Filter by agent status. Omit or use "all" for every agent.

include_tasks.description: Include each agent's claimed_tasks list in the response. Defaults to false.

tools.name: handoff_overview
tools.description: Cross-worktree overview of a single project's multi-agent state: registered agents, a task x agent claim matrix, and a worktree x branch x session mapping. Call from the primary worktree to monitor every worktree working the same project. Works with zero registered agents/claims (single-WT environments).

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

tools.name: handoff_reclaim_task
tools.description: Forcibly release a task's claim lease as a management operation, regardless of which agent holds it or whether the lease has expired (no ownership check, unlike handoff_release_task). Reverts the task to todo and records a task.reclaimed event in events.jsonl. Fails if the task has no active lock.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

task_id.description: Task ID to reclaim.

reason.description: Optional free-text reason for reclaiming, recorded in the events.jsonl entry and echoed back in the response.

tools.name: handoff_events
tools.description: Query .handoff/events.jsonl (lease/agent/session lifecycle events: task.claimed, task.released, task.expired, task.reclaimed, agent.registered, session.created, session.closed) with optional filters. Returns matching events oldest-first, most-recent-first when truncated by limit.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only events at or after this time are returned.

task_id.description: Only events for this task.

event_type.description: Only events of this kind, e.g. "task.claimed".

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return, keeping the most recent. Defaults to 100.

tools.name: handoff_report
tools.description: Report engine (FR-513/SPEC-513): generate Markdown reports from Handlebars templates and run them through an approval workflow. Built-in templates are embedded in the binary; a `<report_type>.md.hbs` file in .handoff/templates/ overrides the built-in of the same name (other *.md.hbs files there are registered too, usable as partials). Templates see `{report: <metadata>, data: <data argument>}`; output is not HTML-escaped. Reports are stored as .handoff/reports/<report_id>.md (body) + <report_id>.json (metadata). action="generate" (write): report_type (required: verification|weekly|inspection|effort|monthly|milestone|defect|completion), scope? ({label?,period?,from?,to?,layers?,items?,campaign?,statuses?,assignee?,milestone?}; unknown keys are an error, and so is a known key the chosen report_type does not use), data? (object passed to the template). report_type=verification (FR-514/SPEC-514) collects its own data: scope.layers / scope.items / scope.campaign / scope.statuses select the rows (campaign rows come from the campaign checklist; otherwise every trace item in the selected layers, using its latest recorded run, a `waive-verify` waiver, or the graph state), and the report has summary counts (the coverage rate is pass/(total-waived), the same covered/(total-na-waived) formula handoff_trace_report and the baseline diff use), per-layer coverage, results with evidence links, failed/blocked items with follow-up tasks, waived items with reasons, and an approval block; keys passed in `data` overlay the collected ones. report_type=weekly (FR-515/SPEC-515) collects its own data for scope.period (ISO week `2026-W41` or range `2026-10-05..2026-10-11`; or scope.from + scope.to; default: the current ISO week; the resolved from/to are stored on the report's scope): tasks completed in the period (completed_at in range, supplemented by `task.status_changed` -> done events in events.jsonl), in-progress tasks with progress and remaining hours, blocked tasks, hours logged in the period (time_log.jsonl) per task vs. estimates and cumulative consumption, per-layer verification progress (from the trace report; a trace failure is rendered, not fatal), milestone progress, and next week's scheduled tasks; keys passed in `data` overlay the collected ones. report_type=inspection (FR-523/SPEC-523, R2: inspection certificate) requires scope.campaign: an APPROVED verification campaign (any other campaign status is an error; layers/items/statuses/period/from/to/assignee are rejected because the certificate covers the whole checklist); it collects its own data and renders document control (document no. `INSP-<campaign id>`, version, issue date, inspectors = checklist verifiers, approver, overall judgement pass|fail|incomplete), revision history, summary counts, the judgement of every checklist item with evidence links (every item is titled with the wording frozen in the campaign checklist, i.e. what was inspected; an item whose current definition differs is flagged `definition changed after inspection` and listed in a Definition Changes After Inspection section with both wordings), non-conforming (failed/blocked) items with follow-up tasks and a blank disposition column, waived items with reasons, and a signature block. report_type=effort (FR-524/SPEC-524, R5: effort report) collects its own data from time_log.jsonl and the task list for scope.period (ISO week or date range) or scope.from + scope.to (default: the whole log) and optional scope.assignee (the entry's agent id, else the task's assignee, else `(unassigned)`; exact match): hours by week and day, by task, by assignee (with share), and an estimate-vs-actual deviation analysis (task schedule estimate vs cumulative actual_hours, variance and variance %, largest first); layers/items/campaign/statuses are rejected; keys passed in `data` overlay the collected ones. Creates a `draft` report; version is 1 + the number of existing reports with the same type and scope. report_type=monthly (FR-531/SPEC-531, R4: monthly report) is the weekly roll-up of scope.period (a calendar month `2026-10`, an ISO week, a range; or scope.from + scope.to; default: the current month; the resolved from/to are stored on the scope) - completed/in-progress/blocked tasks, hours, milestone progress, per-layer verification progress, a per-ISO-week breakdown clipped to the month - plus the trend of the daily metrics snapshots (.handoff/metrics_snapshots/) inside it with the first-to-last change; layers/items/campaign/statuses/assignee/milestone are rejected. report_type=milestone (FR-531/SPEC-531, R6: milestone report) requires scope.milestone (a milestone in config.toml or one a task's schedule.milestone names; anything else is an error; every other scope field is rejected): planned vs actual date (actual = latest completion once every task is done/skipped) with status achieved|achieved_late|overdue|on_track|no_date|no_tasks, its tasks with due/completed dates, delay and estimate-vs-actual hours, bug counts and open bugs (label `bug`), and the project-wide verification state. report_type=defect (FR-531/SPEC-531, R7: defect register) lists tasks labelled `bug` (disposition from a `bug:<fix|defer|waive|not_a_bug>` label, severity = task priority, linked trace items via requirement links) with counts by status/severity/disposition, and the trace items currently failing with their bug tasks (failing items without an open bug are counted); scope.period/from/to (bug created_at), scope.assignee, scope.layers and scope.items narrow it (layers/items keep bugs linked to a matching item and the matching failing items); campaign/statuses/milestone are rejected; a trace graph that cannot be built is rendered, not fatal, unless layers/items need it. report_type=completion (FR-531/SPEC-531, R8: completion report) is refused unless the trace report's project_status is `complete` (every layer approved) and writes nothing otherwise; it integrates project dates and task totals, per-layer verification, milestones, the defect register, effort vs estimate by assignee, and the approved/published reports; only scope.label is accepted. For all of these, keys passed in `data` overlay the collected ones. A custom template that fails to compile is an error (no silent fallback). Returns {report:<metadata>,custom_templates:[names loaded from .handoff/templates/]}. action="list" (read-only): optional report_type and status filters; newest first. Returns {reports:[<metadata>],warnings:[unreadable metadata files]}. action="get" (read-only): report_id (required). Returns {report:<metadata>,body:<markdown>}. action="submit" (write): report_id; draft|revision_requested -> submitted. action="approve" (write): report_id, reviewer? (defaults to the calling agent id; required when neither is known), comment?; submitted -> approved, sets reviewer and approved_at. action="reject" (write): report_id, reviewer? (as above), comment (required reason); submitted -> revision_requested. action="publish" (write): report_id, comment?; approved -> published (terminal; reviewer and approved_at are kept). Any other transition is an error and changes nothing. Metadata: {report_id,report_type,scope,version,status (draft|submitted|approved|revision_requested|published),generated_at,reviewer,approved_at,output_path,revision_history:[{ts,from?,to,actor?,comment?}]}.

project_dir.description: Project directory path. Defaults to current working directory.

period.description: report_type=weekly|effort|monthly|defect: covered period as an ISO week (2026-W41, Monday..Sunday) or an inclusive date range (2026-10-05..2026-10-11); report_type=monthly also takes a calendar month (2026-10). Mutually exclusive with from/to.

from.description: Period start, YYYY-MM-DD (report_type=weekly|effort|monthly|defect: must be given together with `to`).

to.description: Period end, YYYY-MM-DD (report_type=weekly|effort|monthly|defect: must be given together with `from`).

campaign.description: report_type=verification: build the report from this verification campaign (test_run_id); its checklist supplies verdicts, evidence and notes. report_type=inspection (required): the approved campaign to certify.

statuses.description: report_type=verification: keep only rows with one of these results.

assignee.description: report_type=effort: only time-log entries of this person (the entry's agent id, else the task's assignee). report_type=defect: only bugs assigned to this person.

milestone.description: report_type=milestone (required): the milestone to report on.

data.description: action=generate: data made available to the template as `data`.

status.description: action=list: only reports in this status.

reviewer.description: action=approve|reject: reviewer name. Defaults to the calling agent id.

comment.description: action=submit|approve|publish: optional note. action=reject: required reason.

instructions:
Handoff MCP server for AI session context persistence. Call handoff_load_context at session start, handoff_save_context at session end.

## Session Start
1. Call handoff_load_context (no args needed — uses cwd)
2. If it returns "not initialized", call handoff_init with the project name
3. If session_guidance is present, call handoff_save_context with session_status='active' to establish a persistent session before starting work
4. Check the `next_actions` array first — these are the previous session's recommended next steps. Do not re-verify work the previous session already completed

## During Work — Progressive Updates
- Use handoff_update_task to create/update tasks as work progresses
- Mark tasks in_progress when starting, done when complete
- Use handoff_check_criterion to check off task done_criteria as each item is verified — do not wait until the task is fully done
- Use handoff_update_session to progressively update the active session: toggle checklist items, append decisions, notes, or context pointers
- When work reaches a point requiring user confirmation, set the task status to review
- Record decisions as they are made, not just at session end

## Session End
1. Call handoff_save_context with:
- summary: one-line description of what was accomplished
- decisions: key decisions made (with reason and confidence)
- blockers: anything preventing progress
- handoff_notes: caution/context/suggestion for the next session
- context_pointers: files and line ranges the next session should look at
